title: Mastering Stock Markets with Efficient Mixture of Diversified Trading Experts

problem.claim: Quantitative stock investment requires accurate market-status prediction and profitable investment decisions.

gap.claim: Existing deep-learning methods have unstable performance and commonly base investment decisions on a single high-uncertainty neural-network predictor, unlike real-world trading-firm workflows.

contributions.claim: AlphaMix is a three-stage mixture-of-experts framework designed to mimic a bottom-up hierarchical trading-strategy workflow.
The framework trains multiple groups of trading experts using an efficient ensemble method and diversified neural-network hyperparameters and initializations.
AlphaMix uses an as-needed router, with-replacement selection, and integrated expert soup to dynamically select experts from the pool.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe AlphaMix as a novel three-stage mixture-of-experts framework for quantitative investment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on US and Chinese stock markets.
The authors report that AlphaMix significantly outperforms many state-of-the-art baselines on seven popular financial criteria.

narrative_sequence.summary: Quantitative stock investment depends on market prediction and profitable decision making.
Deep-learning trading methods are unstable, and single-predictor decision making has high uncertainty and does not match trading-firm practice.
AlphaMix addresses the gap with a three-stage mixture-of-experts framework involving efficient expert training, diversity construction, and dynamic expert selection.
The authors report superior performance across experiments on US and Chinese stock markets and seven financial criteria.

source_observation.claim: The paper combines expert diversity with a later dynamic selection stage rather than relying on one neural-network predictor.

interpretation.claim: Separating diverse candidate generation from context-dependent selection may address instability caused by dependence on a single model configuration.

application.claim: For uncertain prediction tasks, consider constructing diverse model pools and adding a selection mechanism that adapts which models contribute to each decision.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy improves performance outside the reported stock-market settings or beyond the authors' experiments.

unknowns: Exact datasets, time periods, preprocessing, and trading assumptions are not specified.
The identities and configurations of baselines and the seven financial criteria are not specified.
No numerical results, statistical tests, ablations, or computational-cost measurements are provided.
